proposed.text: An architect places warning tactile domes along a transit platform. BP 344 specifies the domes must be a 600 mm deep field set parallel to and at a specific distance from the platform edge. What is that distance?

options.text: 150 mm away from the platform edge, parallel to the edge along its full length
600 mm away from the platform edge, parallel to the edge along its full length
300 mm away from the platform edge, parallel to the edge along its full length
500 mm away from the platform edge, parallel to the edge along its full length

rationale.summary: Warning tactile domes: 600 mm deep field, placed 300 mm from the platform edge.
rationale.explanation: The 600 mm deep tactile dome field is placed 300 mm back from the platform edge — this is the same 600/300 rule applied at escalator entries. The 300 mm setback gives a user approaching the edge a 300 mm safety buffer after detecting the tactile warning before reaching the drop. Placing domes at 600 mm from the edge creates an excessively large exclusion zone and is not the specified distance.
common_misconceptions: Swapping depth and setback: placing the domes 600 mm from the edge with a 300 mm field
Using 150 mm or 500 mm setback distances not found in BP 344

proposed.explanation: Warning tactile domes at platform edges: 600 mm deep field, set 300 mm from the edge per BP 344.
